title: 78th Nakba Day: Palestinians Mark 1948 Mass Expulsion Amid Intensifying Gaza War
detail: Palestinians worldwide marked the 78th anniversary of the Nakba ('catastrophe') on May 15, 2026 — the 1948 mass displacement of approximately 750,000 Palestinians during the founding of the State of Israel. This year's commemoration came on Day 947 of the Israel-Gaza war, with Nakba Day protests organized in over 60 cities globally including London (projected 500,000+), Paris, New York, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Amman. In Gaza itself, Palestinians displaced for the 6th or 7th time since October 2023 marked the day amid Israeli air and ground strikes. The Washington Post reported Palestinians in Gaza saying 'today's catastrophe is worse' than the original Nakba, citing the combination of mass killing, famine, disease outbreaks, and deliberate infrastructure destruction. Al Jazeera's gallery coverage documented 'millions of Palestinians marking 78 years since the Nakba' — the largest global commemorations in years. The Israeli government did not comment officially on Nakba Day. Solace Global's risk assessment issued prior to the date warned of significant protest activity in major cities and potential security incidents at Israeli embassies and consulates. Palestinian flags, kufiyyas, and maps of pre-1948 Palestine were prominent in the marches, alongside calls for an immediate Gaza ceasefire and ICC enforcement of the arrest warrant against Netanyahu.

media.caption: Millions mark 78th anniversary of Nakba across the world as Gaza war enters Day 947

title: UN Security Council Holds Open Debate on Gaza Ceasefire Consolidation and Escalating Violence (SC16284)
detail: The UN Security Council convened an open debate on May 15, 2026 (UN document SC16284) on ceasefire consolidation in Gaza, escalating Israeli settlement activity in the West Bank, and the overall violence trajectory. The debate came one day after Board of Peace Director General Nickolay Mladenov warned that Gaza risks permanent territorial partition — that the IDF's 'Orange Line' now controls approximately 64% of Gaza and that continued military expansion could create 'a fence or a wall' turning the ceasefire line into a de facto border. At the Security Council, UN Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khiari delivered a briefing documenting: 875+ Palestinians killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect (including 200+ children), continued restricted humanitarian access, and the collapse of Phase 2 ceasefire negotiations. The US (through Ambassador Mike Waltz) reiterated that Hamas must disarm for any sustainable peace. Russia and China criticized Western support for ongoing Israeli operations as inconsistent with ceasefire commitments. France, the UK, and Germany called for de-escalation while expressing support for the Board of Peace governance framework. Palestine's observer status delegation urged immediate enforcement of the November 2024 ICJ order requiring Israel to allow full humanitarian access. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk separately issued a statement calling on Israel to immediately halt plans to take over all of Gaza, warning such plans would constitute a crime under international law.

media.caption: UN Security Council open debate SC16284: ceasefire consolidation, settlement activity, and escalating Gaza violence — May 15, 2026

title: IDF Continues Intensive Strikes Across Gaza on Day 5 of Renewed Military Campaign — Dozens Killed
detail: Israeli air and ground operations continued across Gaza on May 15, 2026 (Day 947 of the war; Day 5 of Israel's renewed military campaign authorized May 10 by the security cabinet). Strikes were concentrated in eastern Gaza City and Khan Younis, the two areas identified by OCHA as facing the highest operational intensity. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, speaking on May 15, stated that a key lesson from October 7 was 'the need for a high and constant level of readiness for a surprise attack on our borders' — remarks widely interpreted as signaling continued aggressive operations. Multiple Palestinian sources reported dozens of Palestinians killed and scores wounded across Gaza throughout the day. Al Jazeera reported a 35% increase in Israeli attacks in April vs. March 2026 (per ACLED data), with the pace intensifying further in the first week of May. Cumulative casualties since the October 2025 ceasefire (now effectively collapsed) stand at approximately 875+ killed and 2,500+ wounded. The total Palestinian death toll since October 7, 2023 has passed 72,750+. UNRWA continued to warn of spreading disease outbreaks, rat infestations, and the collapse of sanitation infrastructure across all five governorates. Egypt's 196th 'Zad Al Izza' humanitarian convoy entered Gaza via the Rafah auxiliary gate on May 14-15, but at 110 trucks/day — a fraction of the 600+ required.

media.caption: IDF continues intensive strikes on Day 5 of renewed campaign across Gaza City and Khan Younis — May 15, 2026

title: Hamas Begins Leadership Succession Process After Mohammed Sinwar Killing — Al-Hayya and Mashaal Emerge as Frontrunners
detail: Two days after the IDF killing of Mohammed Sinwar (Hamas Gaza military commander, May 13, 2026), Hamas began its internal leadership succession process. Multiple intelligence and media assessments published around May 15, 2026 identified two frontrunners for the new Hamas chief position: Khalil al-Hayya (senior Hamas political official and lead ceasefire negotiator, based in Qatar and reported to be operating under a US safety guarantee from the Trump administration) and Khaled Mashaal (former Hamas political bureau chief, diaspora leadership figure based in Turkey/Qatar). A third potential candidate, Sinwar's former deputy in Gaza, was reportedly under consideration but faced internal objections due to his proximity to the decimated military chain of command. The Hamas political bureau was expected to convene an extraordinary session in Doha to select an interim leader within weeks. Al-Hayya was seen as the pragmatic choice favored by Qatar's mediation role and potentially more willing to engage in negotiated disarmament discussions — though Hamas publicly rejected disarmament as 'not on the table' on May 2, 2026. Mashaal represented the more ideological, hardline wing with broader diaspora support. Israeli officials stated the leadership succession was 'irrelevant' as long as Hamas's military infrastructure remained intact. The IDF's stated goal remains destroying Hamas's military and governing capacity in Gaza entirely — not negotiating its political succession.

media.caption: Hamas begins succession process after Sinwar killing — al-Hayya and Mashaal frontrunners for new Hamas chief
